title: AKS Cluster Health

controlTest.positiveScenario: Inject sample events matching UC-4.2.7 SPL; confirm the search returns rows and alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign traffic without matching markers; confirm UC-4.2.7 search returns zero rows.

dataSources: `index=azure` sourcetype=`mscs:azure:diagnostics` collected via `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices`, Splunk OTel Collector; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=azure sourcetype="mscs:azure:diagnostics" Category="kube-apiserver" level="Error"

description: AKS cluster health monitoring ensures Kubernetes workloads are running reliably on Azure's managed platform.
value: Detecting aks cluster health early reduces mean time to contain cloud incidents, supports audit logging controls, and prevents silent misconfiguration drift across accounts.
implementation: Enable AKS diagnostic logging to Event Hub (kube-apiserver, kube-controller-manager, kube-scheduler, kube-audit). Deploy OTel Collector in the AKS cluster for deeper K8s-level monitoring (see Category 3.2).
knownFalsePositives: This pattern can surge during change windows, in sandboxes, and when a platform is in maintenance, so we line alerts up with the calendar and take a second look before we call it an incident.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=azure`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices`, Splunk OTel Collector with the modular input for `mscs:azure:diagnostics`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.2.58.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Enable AKS diagnostic logging to Event Hub (kube-apiserver, kube-controller-manager, kube-scheduler, kube-audit). Deploy OTel Collector in the AKS cluster for deeper K8s-level monitoring (see Category 3.2).
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=azure sourcetype="mscs:azure:diagnostics" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=azure sourcetype="mscs:azure:diagnostics" Category="kube-apiserver" level="Error"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.2.7_aks_cluster_health_7"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `mscs:azure:diagnostics` in `index=azure` to detect aks cluster health. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_2_7_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Status panel, Error timeline, Table..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices`, Splunk OTel Collector and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of aks cluster health so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
